_readme: Conventions: spellings somebody DECIDED on, not spellings somebody SAW.
This is the deliberate opposite of corpus/attested.json. An attested
entry records a sighting and cites a source; a convention has no
source, because nobody has seen the word written — it is how you think
it should be spelled. So conventions never enter the corpus: build
keeps them under their own key in corpus.js, apart from `words`, and
the site draws them WITHOUT the attested underline.
They still carry the finished BLOCK STRUCTURE, flattened two slots per
block, in IPA — same shape as a corpus entry, and same whole-blocks
rule (even token count, nulls written out). That is the point: it lets
a convention pin a spelling the phoneme-only EXCEPTIONS table in
g2p.js cannot, like kyoshi's null and its final /ɪ/.
In the lookup chain a convention wins just below the attested corpus
and above everything derived — so the tool spells the word your way,
but a genuine sighting still outranks a guess. One word gets one
convention; if you disagree with yourself, finish deciding.
Edit this file, or use the workbench: python3 tools/corpus_server.py

conventions.note: The model reads the final vowel as /i/ (ee); it should be /ɪ/ (i). Unsourced — no sample of the name written has turned up yet.
